import sys, json

# The file space's TOOL ADAPTER (GH #908): a model's `tool_call` in, a request
# to `./read`, `./write`, `./ws` or `./derive` out, and that cell's one answer
# back as one `tool_result` under the call's id. Nothing is parked: the call id
# IS the request's `op_id` (every answer mirrors it), so route + `op_id` find the
# call again without a store row (B1 README 2.2) -- and a request whose answer
# never comes leaves no orphan behind in this cell (B1-PP-14).
#
# Two refusals are answered here and reach no other cell: an argument that does
# not match the tool's schema (`bad_request`, OR-FJ-63), and a write or workspace
# op from a surface other than the reasoning core (`read_only`, OR-FJ-L2).
ME = "tools"
# --8<-- file-offer
# THE FILE TOOLS, one list, one entry per tool (GH #908). It stands WORD FOR
# WORD in `./schemas` (which hands it to a model's menu) and in `./tools` (which
# checks every call against it before a request leaves), because a code cell
# has no library it could share: `gh908_every_file_tool_maps_to_one_op.rs`
# holds the two copies to one value. The name IS the mapping: `file_<op>` asks
# the op `<op>`, `file_ws_<x>` the op `ws_<x>`; no other rule exists.
#
# Every description says the two things a model gets wrong without them: how a
# file is addressed, and that the `version` of an answer is the token a write
# has to pass back as `base` (a write against a moved head is merged or refused
# with `base_moved`, never applied blind). `raw`, `ws_tree` and the projection
# ops are deliberately NOT here: bytes and disk projections are no model's
# business in this wave.
ADDR = {"type": "string",
        "description": "the file: `fh-<12 hex>` or a path like `/notes/a.md`, "
                       "optionally with `@<version>`, `@ws:<name>` or `@snap:<name>`"}
WS = {"type": "string",
      "description": "the name of an open workspace to act in (optional)"}
BASE = {"type": "string",
        "description": "the `version` token of the answer this change was made against"}
FORCE = {"type": "boolean",
         "description": "skip the syntax hook (optional)"}
LINE = {"type": "integer", "description": "a 1-based line number"}


def _obj(props, required):
    return {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required,
            "additionalProperties": False}


FILE_OFFER = [
    {"name": "file_info",
     "description": "Describe a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) -- path, kind, size, "
                    "summary line, snapshots -- and name its current `version`, the token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "ws": WS}, ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_read",
     "description": "Read lines `from`..`to` (1-based, negative counts from the end) or one "
                    "`page` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path), each line as "
                    "`<n>:<h4>|<text>`; the answer's `version` is the token a write passes "
                    "back as `base`, and `more` names the next range when it was cut.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "from": LINE, "to": LINE,
                         "page": {"type": "integer", "description": "a page, from 1"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_search",
     "description": "Search one file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) for a `pattern` -- "
                    "`exact`, `regex` or `semantic` -- and list the matching lines with their "
                    "`<n>:<h4>` marks and the `version` token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "pattern": {"type": "string", "description": "what to look for"},
                         "mode": {"type": "string", "enum": ["exact", "regex", "semantic"]},
                         "context": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 2,
                                     "description": "lines around each hit"},
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                                   "description": "the most hits"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file", "pattern"])},
    {"name": "file_summary",
     "description": "The summary of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path), one line or "
                    "`short`, with the `version` token it describes -- the token a write "
                    "passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "level": {"type": "string", "enum": ["oneline", "short"]}},
                        ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_ask",
     "description": "Ask a question about one file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) and get "
                    "an answer with the line ranges it rests on and the `version` token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "question": {"type": "string", "description": "the question"}},
                        ["file", "question"])},
    {"name": "file_history",
     "description": "The history of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path), newest first: "
                    "every move of its main line with op, time and version, and the current "
                    "`version` token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 200}},
                        ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_show",
     "description": "Show one version of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path): size, "
                    "author, parent and its first lines; its `version` is a token a write can "
                    "pass back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "version": {"type": "string", "description": "a version prefix"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file"])},
    {"name": "file_diff",
     "description": "The unified diff of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) between "
                    "version `a` and version `b` (or the current state), with the `version` "
                    "token a write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR,
                         "a": {"type": "string", "description": "the older version"},
                         "b": {"type": "string", "description": "the newer version (optional)"},
                         "ws": WS}, ["file", "a"])},
    {"name": "file_list",
     "description": "List the files and folders under a path `prefix`, each file with its "
                    "address `fh-<12 hex>`; reading one of them names the `version` token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"prefix": {"type": "string", "description": "a folder, `/` by default"},
                         "depth": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1},
                         "ws": WS}, [])},
    {"name": "file_find",
     "description": "Find files whose path matches a `glob` like `/notes/*.md`, each with its "
                    "address `fh-<12 hex>`; reading one of them names the `version` token a "
                    "write passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"glob": {"type": "string"},
                         "limit": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 500},
                         "ws": WS}, ["glob"])},
    {"name": "file_create",
     "description": "Create a file at a new `path` from `text` (or `b64` bytes); the answer "
                    "names its address `fh-<12 hex>` and the `version` token the next write "
                    "passes back as `base`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"path": {"type": "string", "description": "an absolute path"},
                         "text": {"type": "string"},
                         "b64": {"type": "string", "description": "the bytes, base64"},
                         "mime": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["path"])},
    {"name": "file_replace",
     "description": "Replace the text `old` with `new` in a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a "
                    "path), exactly `expected` times (1 by default, or `all`), against the "
                    "`base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE,
                         "old": {"type": "string"}, "new": {"type": "string"},
                         "expected": {"type": ["integer", "string"],
                                      "description": "how many matches: a number or `all`"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "old", "new"])},
    {"name": "file_replace_regex",
     "description": "Replace every match of a regular expression `pattern` with `repl` in a "
                    "file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path), `expected` times, against the "
                    "`base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE,
                         "pattern": {"type": "string"}, "repl": {"type": "string"},
                         "expected": {"type": ["integer", "string"],
                                      "description": "how many matches: a number or `all`"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "pattern", "repl"])},
    {"name": "file_replace_lines",
     "description": "Replace lines `from`..`to` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "with `new`, naming each old line's `h4` mark from the read in `hashes`, "
                    "against the `base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version`.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "from": LINE, "to": LINE,
                         "hashes": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
                         "new": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS},
                        ["file", "base", "from", "to", "hashes", "new"])},
    {"name": "file_insert",
     "description": "Insert `text` before or after `line` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or "
                    "a path) against the `base` token you read; the answer carries the new "
                    "`version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "line": LINE,
                         "where": {"type": "string", "enum": ["before", "after"]},
                         "text": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "line", "text"])},
    {"name": "file_delete",
     "description": "Delete lines `from`..`to` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "against the `base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` "
                    "token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "from": LINE, "to": LINE,
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "from", "to"])},
    {"name": "file_overwrite",
     "description": "Replace the whole content of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "with `text` (or `b64` bytes) against the `base` token you read; the "
                    "answer carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "text": {"type": "string"},
                         "b64": {"type": "string"}, "force": FORCE, "ws": WS},
                        ["file", "base"])},
    {"name": "file_patch",
     "description": "Apply a unified `diff` to a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "against the `base` token you read; the answer carries the new `version` "
                    "token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "diff": {"type": "string"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "diff"])},
    {"name": "file_snapshot",
     "description": "Give the current version of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) a "
                    "`name`, readable later as `@snap:<name>`; the answer names the `version` "
                    "token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "name": {"type": "string"}, "ws": WS},
                        ["file", "name"])},
    {"name": "file_revert",
     "description": "Make an earlier `version` of a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) "
                    "its current one again, against the `base` token you read; the answer "
                    "carries the new `version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE,
                         "version": {"type": "string", "description": "the version to restore"},
                         "force": FORCE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base", "version"])},
    {"name": "file_remove",
     "description": "Remove a file (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path) against the `base` token "
                    "(the `version` you read); its versions stay readable by address.",
     "parameters": _obj({"file": ADDR, "base": BASE, "ws": WS}, ["file", "base"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_open",
     "description": "Open a workspace `name` over the files under `root`: pass its name as "
                    "`ws` to reads and writes (address `fh-<12 hex>` or a path, `base` = the "
                    "`version` token you read) until it is committed or discarded.",
     "parameters": _obj({"name": {"type": "string",
                                  "description": "letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`"},
                         "root": {"type": "string", "description": "a folder, `/` by default"}},
                        ["name"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_status",
     "description": "The files a workspace `ws` touched, each with its address `fh-<12 hex>`, "
                    "state and its `base` and working `version` tokens.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS}, ["ws"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_diff",
     "description": "The unified diff of everything a workspace `ws` changed against the "
                    "versions it started from (files by address `fh-<12 hex>`, each with its "
                    "`version` token).",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS}, ["ws"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_patch",
     "description": "Apply a unified `diff` over several files (by path) inside a workspace "
                    "`ws`; the answer names every moved file's address `fh-<12 hex>` and new "
                    "`version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS, "diff": {"type": "string"}}, ["ws", "diff"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_merge",
     "description": "Merge what moved on the main line since a workspace `ws` opened into it; "
                    "the answer names every merged file's address `fh-<12 hex>`, its new "
                    "`version` token and any conflict.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS}, ["ws"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_commit",
     "description": "Commit a workspace `ws` onto the main line, all files or none, with a "
                    "`note`; the answer names each file's address `fh-<12 hex>` and new "
                    "`version` token.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS, "note": {"type": "string"}}, ["ws"])},
    {"name": "file_ws_discard",
     "description": "Discard a workspace `ws` and everything written in it; the main line and "
                    "its `version` tokens (files by address `fh-<12 hex>`) stay as they are.",
     "parameters": _obj({"ws": WS}, ["ws"])},
]
# --8<-- end file-offer

# The lane a tool's op is served on. Derived from the name, never listed per
# tool: `file_ws_*` -> `in_ws`, the eleven content ops -> `in_write`, every other
# name -> `in_read`. `ask` and a `semantic` search go to `./derive` on the same
# lane, by the condition the hive's own `in_read` edge carries.
WRITE_OPS = ("create", "replace", "replace_regex", "replace_lines", "insert", "delete",
             "overwrite", "patch", "snapshot", "revert", "remove")
# Only the reasoning core writes (OR-FJ-L2): the assistant level stamps
# `context.tool_caller` on every tool edge it draws, and a write that does not
# come from `cogny` is refused here even when a menu offered it by mistake.
WRITER = "cogny"
TYPES = {"string": (str,), "integer": (int,), "number": (int, float),
         "boolean": (bool,), "array": (list,), "object": (dict,)}


def op_of(name):
    """(`op`, lane) of a tool name, or (None, None) for a name this space does
    not serve."""
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.startswith("file_"):
        return None, None
    if name not in [t["name"] for t in FILE_OFFER]:
        return None, None
    op = name[len("file_"):]
    if op.startswith("ws_"):
        return op, "in_ws"
    if op in WRITE_OPS:
        return op, "in_write"
    return op, "in_read"


def type_ok(v, t):
    if isinstance(t, list):
        return any(type_ok(v, x) for x in t)
    want = TYPES.get(t)
    if want is None:
        return True
    # A JSON `true` is no number: python counts bool as int, a schema does not.
    if isinstance(v, bool) and t != "boolean":
        return False
    return isinstance(v, want)


def check(schema, v, at="arguments"):
    """The problems of `v` against a JSON Schema of the subset `FILE_OFFER`
    uses (type, enum, minimum, maximum, required, properties,
    additionalProperties, items); [] when it holds. B1-PP-12 (OR-FJ-63): a
    model's `limit: "ten"` reached `./read`, whose `int()` died without an
    answer -- a tool argument is typed HERE, before any request leaves."""
    out = []
    t = schema.get("type")
    if t is not None and not type_ok(v, t):
        return ["%s must be %s" % (at, t if isinstance(t, str) else " or ".join(t))]
    if "enum" in schema and v not in schema["enum"]:
        out.append("%s must be one of %s" % (at, ", ".join(map(str, schema["enum"]))))
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool):
        if "minimum" in schema and v < schema["minimum"]:
            out.append("%s must be at least %s" % (at, schema["minimum"]))
        if "maximum" in schema and v > schema["maximum"]:
            out.append("%s must be at most %s" % (at, schema["maximum"]))
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        props = schema.get("properties") or {}
        for k in schema.get("required") or []:
            if k not in v:
                out.append("%s.%s is required" % (at, k))
        for k, x in v.items():
            if k in props:
                out.extend(check(props[k], x, "%s.%s" % (at, k)))
            elif schema.get("additionalProperties") is False:
                out.append("%s.%s is not an argument of this tool" % (at, k))
    if isinstance(v, list) and isinstance(schema.get("items"), dict):
        for i, x in enumerate(v):
            out.extend(check(schema["items"], x, "%s[%d]" % (at, i)))
    return out


def request_of(name, args):
    """The request a valid call becomes: (lane, hop, body). `file` goes into the
    body, `ws` onto the hop (a workspace NAME, OR-FH-81; `./read` reads it
    nowhere else), `mode` of a search onto the hop as well (the `in_read` edge
    that picks `./derive` reads it there), everything else into `args`."""
    op, lane = op_of(name)
    rest = {k: v for k, v in args.items() if k not in ("file", "ws")}
    body = {"op": op, "args": rest}
    if "file" in args:
        body["file"] = args["file"]
    hop = {"route": lane, "op": op}
    if args.get("ws"):
        hop["ws"] = args["ws"]
    if op == "search" and args.get("mode"):
        hop["mode"] = args["mode"]
    return lane, hop, body


def result_text(answer):
    """A space's answer as the text a model reads: the answer's own fields, the
    correlation (`op_id`, `caller`) and the transport (`messages`) removed.
    Nothing is cut here: `./read` already caps what one answer carries."""
    keep = {k: v for k, v in answer.items()
            if k not in ("op_id", "caller", "messages", "header")}
    return json.dumps(keep, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)


def refusal(op, code, message):
    return {"ok": False, "op": op or "", "error": {"code": code, "message": message}}


def tool_result(call_id, answer):
    head = {"route": "tool_result", "tool_call_id": call_id}
    if answer.get("ok") is False:
        head["error_code"] = str((answer.get("error") or {}).get("code") or "")
    return {"header": head,
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": call_id,
                          "text": result_text(answer)}]}


# Review L m-1: a provider's call ids are unique only within one answer (stubs
# and local servers repeat `call_0`), and B1 parks under (`op_id`, cell) -- the
# request carries the call id under this cell's own prefix (the projection's
# `git:` form, OR-FJ-68), the answer finds the call id again without it.
PREFIX = ME + ":"


def call_of(op_id):
    op_id = str(op_id or "")
    return op_id[len(PREFIX):] if op_id.startswith(PREFIX) else op_id


def translate(name, raw, call_id, tool_caller):
    """One tool call -> the ONE message this cell emits for it: the request, or
    a `tool_result` that refuses it without asking any cell."""
    op, lane = op_of(name)
    if op is None:
        return tool_result(call_id, refusal("", "tool_unknown",
                                            "this file space has no tool %r" % (name,)))
    if isinstance(raw, dict):
        args = raw
    else:
        try:
            args = json.loads(raw or "{}")
        except Exception:
            args = None
    if not isinstance(args, dict):
        return tool_result(call_id, refusal(op, "bad_request",
                                            "the arguments are not a JSON object"))
    if lane != "in_read" and tool_caller != WRITER:
        return tool_result(call_id, refusal(
            op, "read_only", "only the reasoning core writes files or opens workspaces; "
                             "this surface reads"))
    schema = [t for t in FILE_OFFER if t["name"] == name][0]["parameters"]
    bad = check(schema, args)
    if bad:
        return tool_result(call_id, refusal(op, "bad_request", "; ".join(bad)))
    if not call_id:
        return tool_result(call_id, refusal(op, "bad_request", "the call carries no id"))
    lane, hop, body = request_of(name, args)
    hop.update({"op_id": PREFIX + call_id, "caller": ME})
    body["header"] = hop
    body["messages"] = []
    return body


doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
h = (doc.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {}
hop = h.get("hop") or {}
ctx = h.get("context") or {}
lane = str(hop.get("route") or "")


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


if lane == "in_tool":
    msgs = d.get("messages") or []
    call = msgs[0] if msgs and isinstance(msgs[0], dict) else {}
    # The id comes from the TURN first and the hop second, as in
    # `memory-hive/tool`: the turn is what the round's fan-in waits on.
    call_id = str(call.get("id") or hop.get("tool_call_id") or "")
    name = str(hop.get("tool_name") or "")
    emit([translate(name, call.get("text"), call_id, str(ctx.get("tool_caller") or ""))])

if lane == "answer":
    if str(hop.get("caller") or "") != ME:
        sys.stderr.write("file-space/tools: an answer for %r -- dropped\n"
                         % str(hop.get("caller") or ""))
        emit([])
    call_id = call_of(hop.get("op_id") or d.get("op_id"))
    emit([tool_result(call_id, d)])

sys.stderr.write("file-space/tools: unknown lane %r -- dropped\n" % lane)
emit([])

description.purpose: The translation between a model's tool round and this space's own lanes: a `file_<op>` call becomes the request `<op>` on `in_read`, `in_write` or `in_ws` of the cell that serves it (`ask` and a semantic search reach `./derive`), under `caller` 'tools' and with the call id as `op_id`; that cell's one answer comes back as one `tool_result` under the call id, its fields as JSON text without `op_id` and `caller`.
description.use_when: Reached on this hive's `in_tool` lane with one tool call (`hop.tool_name`, the arguments as JSON text in the turn), and on `answer` from `./read`, `./write`, `./ws` or `./derive` when `hop.caller` is 'tools'.
description.not_in_scope: No store and nothing parked: the call id IS the request's `op_id`, so route and `op_id` find the call again. No shortening of an answer (`./read` caps what one answer carries). No `raw`, `ws_tree` or projection op.
description.emits_meaning: A request on `in_read`/`in_write`/`in_ws` (hop `op`, `op_id` = the call id, `caller` 'tools', `ws` the workspace name, `mode` of a search), or `tool_result` with `tool_call_id` (and `error_code` when `ok` is false). Refused without asking any cell: an argument that does not match the tool's schema (`bad_request`), and a write or workspace op when `context.tool_caller` is not 'cogny' (`read_only`).
description.consumes_meaning: A tool call, and the answers of the space's cells to the requests this cell sent.
